steps.description: Click the "General Teams Agent" option in the dropdown menu within the "Teams Agent or App Using Teams AI Library" dialog.
Click the "Simple Bot" option in the "Teams Capability" dropdown menu.
Click on the "JavaScript" option in the "Programming Language" dropdown menu within the Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit interface at coordinates (288, 101).
Click the "Default folder" field in the "Workspace Folder" dialog to select the path "/home/vscode/AgentsToolkitProjects".
Click the "Close" (X) button at the top-right corner of the Microsoft Teams web app window in Google Chrome to close the tab.
Click the "Close" (X) button at the top-right corner of the Microsoft Visual Studio Code window to close the application.
Click the "Create a Agent/App" button in the left sidebar of the Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit extension panel within Visual Studio Code.
Click the "Other Teams Capabilities" option in the dropdown menu within the "Teams Agent or App Using Microsoft Teams SDK" interface in Visual Studio Code.

Click the "Simple Bot" option in the dropdown menu under "Teams Capability" within the Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit extension for Visual Studio Code. The selected option is visually highlighted with a red crosshair, confirming the interaction point.
Click the "TypeScript" option in the "Programming Language" dropdown menu within the Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit extension interface in Visual Studio Code.
Click the "Default folder" option in the workspace folder selection dropdown within Visual Studio Code, choosing the directory `/home/vscode/AgentsToolkitProjects` for the project location.
Type #text:${{var:app_name:vscuse_app_#####}}abc into the "Application Name" input field at the top of the Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit interface in Visual Studio Code.
Press the Enter key to confirm the input in the command palette text field at the top of the Visual Studio Code window while working in the Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit extension.
Click the "env" folder in the EXPLORER file tree of Visual Studio Code to expand or select it.
Activate the integrated terminal in Visual Studio Code by pressing the keyboard shortcut Ctrl+` while viewing the workspace and README.md preview.
Type text: 'cp ' into the integrated terminal (bash) at the bottom of the Visual Studio Code window within the project.
Type #text:~/AgentsToolkitProjects/${{var:app_name:vscuse_app_#####}}/env/.env.local into the integrated Bash terminal at the bottom of the Visual Studio Code window, within the project workspace.
Type the text ' ./env/' into the active Bash terminal within Visual Studio Code's integrated terminal panel.
Press the Enter key in the Visual Studio Code integrated terminal to execute the command.
Type text: 'cp ' into the integrated terminal input field at the bottom of the Visual Studio Code application.
Type #text:~/AgentsToolkitProjects/${{var:app_name:vscuse_app_#####}}/env/.env.local.user into the integrated Bash terminal of Visual Studio Code on the workspace.
Type the text ` ./env/` into the integrated terminal at the bottom of the Visual Studio Code window, within a Bash session in the workspace.
Press the Enter key in the VS Code integrated terminal after typing the command to execute the file copy operation.
Toggle the integrated terminal panel in Visual Studio Code by pressing **Ctrl+`** while viewing the workspace, with a README preview open and the file explorer visible.
Click the ".env.local" file in the "env" folder within the Explorer panel of Visual Studio Code to open the environment configuration file.
Click the "T" in "TEAMS_APP_ID" within the `.env.local` file opened in the VS Code editor, targeting line 9, column 7.
Use keyboard shortcut Ctrl+/ in Visual Studio Code to toggle line comment on the selected lines within the `.env.local` file in the editor pane.
Click the "BOT_MAIN" environment variable value in the `.env.local` file within the editor pane of Visual Studio Code.

Trigger the keyboard shortcut Ctrl+/ in Visual Studio Code while the ".env.local" file in the "env" folder is open and active in the editor. This action will comment or uncomment the selected lines in the file based on their current state.
Click the left mouse button on the "BOT_ENDPOINT" variable in the .env.local file within the VS Code editor, specifically at the URL value.
Use keyboard shortcut Ctrl+/ in Visual Studio Code to toggle commenting on the selected lines within the ".env.local" file in the editor pane.
Click the "TEAMS_APP_TENANT_ID" value field in the `.env.local` file opened within Visual Studio Code, placing the cursor in the text editor for environment variable editing.
Use keyboard shortcut: ctrl+/ to toggle comment on the selected line (TEAMS_APP_TENANT_ID) in the .env.local file within Visual Studio Code's editor pane.

Click on the text field in the Visual Studio Code editor at line 13, column 9 within the ".env.local" file, specifically on the "BOT_OBJECT_ID" variable, to place the cursor after "BOT_OBJECT_ID=" for editing environment variable values.
Use keyboard shortcut: ctrl+/ to toggle comment on the selected line (BOT_OBJECT_ID) in the .env.local file within the VS Code editor.
Use the keyboard shortcut "Ctrl+End" to move the cursor to the end of the ".env.local" file currently open in the Visual Studio Code editor within the workspace.
Press the Enter key at the end of line 13 in the `.env.local` file within Visual Studio Code, adding a new line to the environment variable configuration.
Type text: 'TEAMS_APP_ID=' into the last line of the .env.local file in the Visual Studio Code editor, within the env folder of the VSExplorer panel.
Press the Enter key while editing the ".env.local" file in Visual Studio Code, specifically at the end of the line containing "TEAMS_APP_ID=" in the editor pane.
Type 'BOT_DOMAIN_ID=' at the end of the '.env.local' file inside the editor pane of Visual Studio Code, within the 'env' folder of the workspace.
Press the Enter key while editing the .env.local file in Visual Studio Code, at the end of line 15 in the environment variables editor.
Type text 'BOT_ENDPOINT=' at the beginning of line 16 in the .env.local file within Visual Studio Code's text editor.
Save changes to the ".env.local" file in the VS Code editor using the Ctrl+S keyboard shortcut.
Click the ".env.local" file in the "env" folder within the VS Code Explorer panel to open its contents.
Click the ".env.local.user" file entry in the Explorer panel within Visual Studio Code to open the environment variable file for editing.
Use keyboard shortcut Ctrl+/ to toggle line comment for the selected text in the `.env.local.user` file within the VS Code editor.
Save changes to the file ".env.local.user" in Visual Studio Code by pressing the keyboard shortcut Ctrl+S while the file is open and active in the editor tab.
